page.layout: One page of text in one column. Running head top right, page number top left. Heading "CONCIO XXV." with reference "Prouerb. 12." below it. Italic epigraph with drop-cap M. Two paragraphs of text. Catchword at the right foot. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: mne opus bonum reprobi, Tit. 1. Virgines fatuæ, Matth. 25. apostatæ, 2. Pet. 2. Hinc Chrysostomus Hom. 17. in Matth. Porcos, inquit, intelligendos puto Christianos car-nalibus & immundis voluptatibus deditos, quoniam propter fidem quidem suam mundi sunt, propter actus autem suos fordidos habentur immundi. Dominus noster Iesus Christus ita nobis adaugeat fidem, ut eam o-stendere possimus ex factis nostris, propter nomen suum sanctum & salutare, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO XXV.
Proverb. 12.

p.i: Mulier sedula corona est mariti sui: sed quasi putredo in ossibus eius est (mulier) confusione digna.

main_text.p: 1 Hoc unum est ex dictis Salomonis, quæ parabolæ & proverbia nuncupantur. Parabolæ quidem sive similitudines, quia occulta sunt, & secreta mysteria significat: Proverbia autem, quia talia sunt, quæ sæpius in ore fidelium versari, ac memoriæ commendari, ac retineri debent. Simus igitur & illius dicti memores, & sciamus id non solum juxta literam esse intelligendum, sed aliter quoque ac spiritualiter.
2 Quæ est ergo sententia simplex huius loci? Mulierem magnum bonum, item ma-gnum malum esse, quemadmodum etiam Chrysostomus testatur in epistola ad Hebr.

page.notes: Top line is a fragment: "mne" begins at the left edge, so the first letter is cut off by the scan. Printed "munedi" at the line break appears to be "mundi" with the hyphen lost; marked as read. "s" and "f" are normalised to s. Small reference marks in the right and left margins beside "Amen." and the sermon heading carry no printed text, so none are transcribed as notes. The "2" of the second paragraph and the "1" of the first are printed numbers, kept as printed. "vbi" at the foot is the catchword, not part of the text.
